NOTE ON TIMING: this edition is late because the scheduled job hung for over an hour and was killed. The
read is therefore nearly three hours after the London close rather than the usual one. Everything is live
or closed; nothing is carried.

*** THE GILT MADE A ROUND TRIP AND THIS MORNING'S FIGURE DID NOT SURVIVE THE DAY ***
This morning's edition published the gilt at 5.38, down six basis points, and the drivers called it "the
sharpest fall in weeks". By the close it is back at 5.4422. The fall was real when it was read at 07:53
and the day erased it. That is the second time in two days an instrument has reversed between our own
editions — Brent did the same thing on Monday — and the honest response is to say so rather than let the
series look smooth.
THE CHANGE IS GENUINELY DISPUTED, AND THE PROVIDERS NOW DISAGREE ON DIRECTION:
  CNBC:              5.4422, change -0.0115 (on prev 5.4537)  -> -0.01
  Trading Economics: 5.45,   day change +0.013               -> +0.01
  Our own series:    5.4422 against Monday's post-close 5.4444 -> -0.0022 -> 0.00
PUBLISHED: 5.44, change 0.00. The level is agreed to within a basis point and the change straddles zero,
so claiming a direction either provider contradicts would be false precision. Note CNBC's previous_day_
closing has drifted again — it read 5.4466 this morning and 5.4537 tonight for the same Monday close.
That field has now been unusable for nine consecutive days.

*** BRENT: RECOVERED THROUGH THE SESSION, STILL LOWER ON THE DAY ***
Read 105.39 at 07:53 and 105.89 at 19:15, against Monday's 106.65. So crude fell early, clawed back about
half of it, and still closed the day down 0.71%. The Houthis threatened Aramco facilities and Saudi
airports this afternoon, which is the obvious candidate for the afternoon bid and which the world column
carries.
CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics 105.82 -0.77% against CNBC 105.89 -0.71%. Agreement. WTI 94.26 +0.55%.
